name: Bodb Derg

attributes.attribute: most powerful magician of the Tuatha Dé Danann
brother of Aonghus Óg, the god of poetry

sources: Joyce, Patrick Weston. Ancient Celtic Romances. London: Parkgate Books, 1997.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Bodb Derg is an Irish god or hero. He was the strongest magician of the Tuatha Dé Danann. He was the son of the good god Dagda. He was also the brother of Aonghus Óg, the god of poetry. He ruled from a great palace on the edge of Lough Derg. The Tuatha Dé elected him king. That choice angered the god Lir. Bodb Derg then punished Aífe. She had enchanted the children of Lir into swans. He turned Aífe into a demon or a crane.

okr.objective: Describe Bodb Derg, the magician whom the Tuatha named king.
